title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Delivers Fast, Accurate Specialized Task Execution for Long-Running Agents | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30B MoE with 3B active parameters licensed under OpenMDW-1.1 with weights, data and recipes, explicitly built for the high-volume execution layer of long-running agents rather than for frontier reasoning. The strategic move alongside it is NeMo Switchyard, a routing library that sends planning up to frontier models like Nemotron 3 Ultra and execution down to Lightning — NVIDIA claiming 86% on PinchBench with 10,000 tasks completed 30% faster than Qwen3.6 35B at similar accuracy, and up to 4x output speed versus similar-sized models.

insights.claim: Developers are increasingly building applications as a system of models where frontier reasoning models such as Nemotron 3 Ultra handle orchestration and planning while smaller efficient models handle the high-volume execution layer.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Token volume is migrating to cheap small models while frontier models keep only the planning share — a direct headwind to per-token pricing power at the frontier.
insights.quote: Frontier reasoning models such as Nemotron 3 Ultra handle orchestration and complex planning while smaller, more efficient models handle the high-volume execution layer.

insights.claim: Long-running AI agents spend most of their time on tool calls, result validation and subagent delegation, so using a frontier reasoning model for every execution step adds cost and latency without adding capability.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: The economic bulk of agentic workloads is routine execution, meaning most inference demand will be served by small models, not frontier ones.
insights.quote: Long-running AI agents spend most of their time on high-volume execution: tool calls, result validation, and subagent delegation. Using a frontier reasoning model for every execution step adds cost and latency.
insights.locator: Long-running AI agents spend most of their time

insights.claim: NeMo Switchyard exposes Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as a routing target alongside a customer's open and closed models, so every request lands on the most capable and efficient model that can handle it — plans route up, execution routes down.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Owning the router is the strategically valuable position: it decides which vendor's model receives each request, and NVIDIA is giving that layer away to seed its own models.
insights.quote: Plans route up to the frontier, execution routes down to Lightning, ensuring that your tokens are spent efficiently and effectively.
insights.locator: Route work to the right model using NeMo Switchyard

insights.claim: NVIDIA frames its open model family as a continuously improving software library rather than discrete releases, positioning model routing and orchestration as rapidly maturing alongside it.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Treating models as versioned library dependencies implies faster substitution cycles and lower switching costs between model vendors.
insights.quote: The NVIDIA Nemotron open model family is like a software library, with each release continuously improving accuracy and speed.
insights.locator: The NVIDIA Nemotron open model family

insights.claim: On PinchBench, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reaches 86% accuracy while completing 10,000 tasks 30% faster than Qwen3.6 35B at similar accuracy.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is now benchmarking head-to-head against Chinese open models at the same parameter class, signalling where it sees the competitive threat in open weights.
insights.quote: On PinchBench, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reaches 86% accuracy while completing 10,000 tasks 30% faster than Qwen3.6 35B at similar accuracy.

insights.claim: NVIDIA claims Nemotron 3.5 Lightning wins the accuracy-versus-speed Pareto frontier on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, a nine-evaluation composite covering agentic tasks, coding, scientific reasoning and general intelligence, with up to 4x the output speed of similar-sized models.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Third-party composite indices are becoming the accepted scoreboard vendors design against — worth tracking as the arbiter of open-model share.
insights.quote: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning combines strong intelligence with up to 4x output speed of similar-sized models, placing it on the accuracy-speed Pareto frontier for high-volume agent workloads.
insights.locator: How does Nemotron 3.5 Lightning perform on the accuracy-speed Pareto frontier?

insights.claim: The proposed metric for agent efficiency is how quickly a model completes useful work, not how fast it generates tokens — reframing evaluation away from raw tokens-per-second.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Task-completion throughput, not token throughput, is the metric that will govern agentic inference procurement and cost modelling.
insights.quote: Agent efficiency ultimately comes down to how quickly a model completes useful work and not simply how fast it generates tokens.

themes.theme: Inference engineering: MTP, draft models, NVFP4

insights.claim: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning underwent a dedicated pretraining stage to bake multi-token prediction into the model plus a post-training MTP-boosting phase, mirroring the approach used for Nemotron 3 Super and Ultra.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Speculative decoding is moving from a serving-time trick into the pretraining recipe, which raises the barrier for third parties trying to retrofit the same speedups.
insights.quote: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning underwent a dedicated pretraining stage to bake multi-token prediction (MTP) into the model, as with Nemotron 3 Super and Ultra.

insights.claim: Two draft models ship alongside the base model with explicit concurrency guidance: DSpark for DGX Spark and low-concurrency data center workloads, MTP for medium-to-high concurrency with optimal draft length falling as concurrency rises, and DFlash as an additional option to benchmark.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Optimal serving configuration now varies by concurrency regime, so published throughput numbers are only meaningful with the load profile attached.
insights.quote: MTP is best suited for medium to high concurrency, with the optimal draft length decreasing as concurrency increases.
insights.locator: Beyond MTP, two draft models are provided

insights.claim: The model ships an NVFP4 checkpoint alongside BF16 using the same specialized NVFP4 kernels that power Nemotron 3 Ultra across Blackwell, Hopper and Ampere GPUs, so one file serves both data centers and desktop DGX Spark.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: NVFP4 support reaching back to Ampere and Hopper extends the useful life of the installed base and makes NVIDIA's numeric format a cross-generation standard.
insights.quote: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning ships with an NVFP4 checkpoint alongside BF16, using the same specialized NVFP4 kernels that power Nemotron 3 Ultra across NVIDIA Blackwell, NVIDIA Hopper, and NVIDIA Ampere GPUs.

insights.claim: The model is explicitly trained for popular agent harnesses such as OpenClaw and Hermes Agent, with harness-optimized training presented as the source of more accurate tool calls at lower latency.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Training against specific harnesses couples model quality to particular agent frameworks, creating a new axis of ecosystem lock-in below the model layer.
insights.quote: The model is trained for popular agent harnesses, enabling agents to make more accurate calls while reducing latency for high-volume tasks.

insights.claim: NVIDIA released weights, training data and recipes under OpenMDW-1.1, including the Nemotron-RL Agentic Terminal Pivot reinforcement learning dataset used to train some of the coding agent capabilities.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Releasing training data and RL environments, not just weights, is a commoditize-your-complement play that undercuts closed model vendors' data advantage.
insights.quote: the weights, training data, and recipes are released as permissively as possible under OpenMDW-1.1
insights.locator: Customize Nemotron 3.5 Lightning out of the box

insights.claim: The 30B/3B-active size is designed to run anywhere from NVIDIA Jetson and a GeForce RTX 5090 to DGX Spark and full data centers, with support across LM Studio, llama.cpp, Ollama and Unsloth.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Capable agentic inference on consumer RTX and edge hardware opens a demand channel outside hyperscaler capex and pulls agent workloads off the cloud metering.
insights.quote: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning makes capable agentic AI accessible on local systems including NVIDIA Jetson, GeForce RTX 5090, and DGX Spark.
insights.locator: How is Nemotron 3.5 Lightning ideal for local AI?

insights.claim: Small models are argued to earn their place through customization economics — they fine-tune faster, cheaper and on far more modest hardware than larger counterparts, supported by LoRA/full SFT via NeMo Automodel and Megatron Bridge and RL via NeMo RL and NeMo Gym.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: The specialization tailwind favors an ecosystem of many fine-tuned small models over a few general frontier APIs, reshaping where inference spend lands.
insights.quote: small models fine-tune faster, cheaper, and on far more modest hardware than their larger counterparts
insights.locator: Models earn their place in specialized AI agent systems

insights.claim: The partner list spans hosted inference providers including CoreWeave, Crusoe, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Baseten, Nebius, Modal and DeepInfra plus hyperscaler platforms Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, MSFT Foundry and OCI Enterprise AI.
insights.speaker: Chris Alexiuk
insights.so_what: Day-one availability across neoclouds and all three hyperscalers means an open NVIDIA model gets frontier-grade distribution without NVIDIA operating the inference itself.
